DiscrepancyLE(f,g,s) means that some real C satisfies f(x)≤g(x)+C for every x in s. DiscrepancyEquiv(f,g,s) requires this bound in both directions. Thus the two functions differ by a bounded amount on s. The notation follows Mochizuki’s correction in IUT IV, Remark 2.3.1(ii), p. 55. Source notation: [GenEll], Definition 1.2(ii), p. 5, with the correction in IUT IV, Remark 2.3.1(ii), p. 55.

**Limits of the definition supplier**

The uncorrected direction printed in [GenEll], Definition 1.2(ii), p. 5 is reversed. Cite the correction when describing ≲.

The two directions may use different constants. A common absolute-value bound follows by taking their maximum.

These definitions introduce relations, not quotient types of BD-classes.

They apply to arbitrary real-valued functions on a type α. No geometric height theory is required to form the relations.

> The relation “$\approx$” clearly defines an equivalence relation on the set of functions $\mathcal F\to\mathbb R$; we shall refer to an equivalence class relative to this equivalence relation as a(n) [$\mathcal F$-]BD-class [i.e., “bounded discrepancy class”].

— Arithmetic Elliptic Curves in General Position, §1, Definition 1.2(ii), sentences after the defining inequality, printed pp. 5.

> In [GenEll], Definition 1.2, (ii), the non-resp’d and first resp’d items in the display should be reversed! That is to say, the notation “$\alpha\lesssim_{\mathcal F}\beta$” corresponds to “$\alpha(x)-\beta(x)\leq C$”; the notation “$\alpha\gtrsim_{\mathcal F}\beta$” corresponds to “$\beta(x)-\alpha(x)\leq C$”.

— Inter-universal Teichmüller Theory IV: Log-volume Computations and Set-theoretic Foundations, §2, Remark 2.3.1(ii), correction of [GenEll], Definition 1.2(ii), printed pp. 55.
